ev.q: In 2006, a total of 13,767 tuberculosis (TB) cases (4.6 per 100,000 population) were reported in the United States
The foreign-born to U.S.-born rate ratio increased 7.0%, from 8.9 in 2005 to 9.5 in 2006.
The U.S.-born TB rate was 2.3 per 100,000 population
The average annual percentage decline in the TB incidence rate decreased from 7.3% per year during 1993--2000
the proportion of MDR-TB cases remained constant at 1.2% from 2004
the percentage of TB cases with HIV infection decreased 4.4% (from 13.0% to 12.4%)
The U.S.-born TB rate was 2.3 per 100,000 population
82.7% of patients for whom < 1 year of treatment was indicated completed therapy within 1 year
The foreign-born to U.S.-born rate ratio increased 7.0%, from 8.9 in 2005 to 9.5 in 2006.
The TB rates among blacks, Asians, and Hispanics † were 8.4, 21.2, and 7.6 times higher than rates among whites
TB is a nationally notifiable disease.
The TB rate in 2006 was the lowest recorded since national reporting began in 1953, but the rate of decline has slowed since 2000.

methods_quotes.q: by using current U.S. census population estimates for the years 1993 through 2006.
California was excluded from the analysis of HIV among TB cases because it reports its HIV data separately
All HIV estimates were based on provisional data.
